key_insight: Across perovskites, polar off-centering enhances low-frequency infrared and dielectric responses, while nonpolar octahedral tilting is associated with Raman central peaks.
engineering_relevance: Linking spectral features to lattice instabilities can guide interpretation of structural dynamics in halide-perovskite solar-cell materials.
method: Simulate infrared and Raman spectra using machine-learning-based molecular dynamics.
Compare seven oxide, halide and double-halide perovskites with polar, tilt-driven or mixed instabilities.
Relate spectral signatures to mode symmetry, coupling strength and dynamics.
evidence_signal: Simulations across seven perovskites link slow polar reorientations to very-low-frequency dielectric responses and overdamped tilting modes to persistent Raman central peaks.
watch_item: The abstract reports no solar-cell device tests or quantitative experimental validation, so photovoltaic performance implications remain unestablished.
paper_title: Unifying Low-Frequency Raman and Infrared Signatures across Perovskites
